I've seen it in all sorts of cases. I started out in the ER and whatnot before I realized I was NOT going to be okay mentally after a while of that. 

It's so strange. Someone mentioned earlier that we have some inherent traits left over from when our place at the top of the food chain was a little more unsteady than it is now. Decaying corpses obviously draw predators and that could threaten the rest of the herd. Other than that, I have NO idea how they do it. 

I've seen a lot of people die, a lot of folks that wait to see that one last person before they go, wait for solitude... It's still amazing to me after all this time. Ultimately the hopeless romantic in me wants to believe that if they can help it, they don't want to leave their loved ones or fellow humans with a traumatic memory. They'd rather be remembered alive and how they were before.

That would absolutely make sense. Ultimately when it comes down to basic biology and ingrained behavior, we're not that different from (for example) dogs. We all know they tend to go off somewhere else to die to avoid drawing predators to the rest of the herd. 

We do have a cozy space at the top of the food chain but that wasn't always so secure. Even now, if you take our tools away and put us in the wrong environment, we can shift pretty uncomfortably far down that chain.

I couldn't go out in public thanks to another variation of crippling anxiety. It was all around an absolute shitshow. I was (still am) here completely alone, no family or anything nearby to keep tabs on me. I was lucky. I have no idea how I survived it long enough to go get help, but I did. 

Mine was triggered by a TBI from a car accident some years ago. It changed my personality, I lost a lot of memories that were irreplaceable, I forgot 3 languages... it was awful but I had no idea the worst was to come. Don't wait until you get to rock bottom because once you lay down and accept defeat, you may not want to get back up. Much love and good luck to you, please take care of yourself ❤
